questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'By next July, the new hospital ___ twenty years of service.'
questions.context: English class in Mejicanos, SV.

options.text: will have been in service
options.feedback: 'Will have been' is the future perfect, and it treats the twenty years as finished by the future deadline.

options.text: is serving
options.feedback: 'Is serving' is the present continuous, so it describes service that is still going on today.

options.text: served
options.feedback: 'Served' is the simple past, which places the service entirely before the moment of speaking.

options.text: has been serving
options.feedback: 'Has been serving' is the present perfect continuous and looks forward from now, not from next July.

questions.explanation: The future perfect is 'will have' plus a past participle, and it presents an activity as complete before a stated future moment. The hospital will have completed twenty years of service by next July, so this is the structure the sentence needs.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence reports that the bridge will already be finished before the road opens?
questions.context: English class in Santa Ana, SV.

options.text: The road will open when the bridge is finished.
options.feedback: 'When' with a future form marks the two events as coinciding, so neither one comes first.

options.text: By the time the road opens, the bridge will have been finished.
options.feedback: 'Will have been finished' places the completed bridge before the future moment the road opens.

options.text: The bridge has already been finished before the road opens.
options.feedback: 'Has been finished' is the present perfect, and it never projects onto a future reference point.

options.text: The bridge will be finished while the road is opening.
options.feedback: 'While' makes the two actions overlap, and an overlapping action cannot precede the other.

questions.explanation: 'By the time' plus a future clause calls for the future perfect. The future perfect, 'will have' plus a past participle, presents the bridge as complete before the road opens, which is precisely the relationship this sentence reports.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read: 'When she looks at the photos, she will remember how quiet the valley was.' What does the sentence predict?
questions.context: English class in Santa Ana, SV.

options.text: The valley will be noisy by the time she sees the photos.
options.feedback: The sentence calls the valley quiet, so the opposite adjective contradicts the text.

options.text: She has already forgotten the valley completely.
options.feedback: 'Will remember' points at the future, so the memory is still available to her afterwards.

options.text: She will recall the valley's quiet once she sees the photos.
options.feedback: 'Will remember' links a future reaction to a later event, and the valley is described as quiet.

options.text: She never visited the valley at all.
options.feedback: The sentence recalls the valley from personal experience, which a visit is implied to have supplied.

questions.explanation: 'Will remember' states a future reaction, so the text predicts what she will think later rather than what she thinks now. The photos trigger the memory, and the quality she recalls is the quiet of the valley, so option C is the supported reading.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which time expression signals that an action is presented as complete before a future point?
questions.context: English class in San Salvador, SV.

options.text: At the end of the concert
options.feedback: 'At the end of' marks a moment, not a completed stretch of time measured up to that moment.

options.text: Every Tuesday afternoon
options.feedback: A habitual schedule like this one is expressed with the simple present or the simple future.

options.text: Just yesterday evening
options.feedback: That expression points at the past, where the future perfect cannot be used at all.

options.text: By the end of next season
options.feedback: 'By' plus a future deadline measures completion up to that point, which is the future perfect's trigger.

questions.explanation: The future perfect needs a reference point in the future, and 'by' with a deadline supplies exactly that. Completion is measured up to the endpoint, so 'By the end of next season' is the expression that pairs with the structure.
questions.subject: ingles

options.feedback: 'After' reverses the order, because the blockage is placed earlier than the inspection of the panel.

options.feedback: 'Had already blocked' presents the blockage as finished before the future moment of the check.

options.text: The technician will never open the panel at all.
options.feedback: The sentence explicitly opens the panel, so refusing to inspect it is not what the text says.
